name: Hosa Aba
description: Hosa Aba (meaning 'Trousers Down') is the Swiss-German variant of the popular European banking game 'Schwimmen' or '31'. It is a fast-paced game of card swapping where players aim to collect cards of a single suit totaling 31 points (Hosa Aba). It is traditionally played with Swiss-German suited cards in the German-speaking cantons of Switzerland.

history.origins: Part of the extensive family of 'Thirty-One' games that have existed in Europe since the 15th century. Hosa Aba specifically refers to the localized Swiss version with its unique terminology.
timeline: 15th Century: 'Thirty-One' games recorded in French and Italian literature.
19th Century: Becomes a staple parlor game in Switzerland and Southern Germany.
Present: Popular in Swiss pubs and family gatherings under various names like 'Schwimmen' or 'Knack'.
history.cultural: Known for the humorous phrase 'Hosa Aba!' shouted when a player achieves 31, forcing others to 'drop their trousers' (equivalent to losing a life).
history.evolution: The game adapted to the 36-card Swiss deck, adding specific values for 'Banner' (10s) and ensuring Ace (11) remains the most powerful card.

setup.deck: 36-card Swiss-German deck (6-10, Under, Ober, King, Ace).
setup.dealing: Deal 3 cards to each player and 3 cards face-down in the center ('The Window').

rules.objective: Avoid having the lowest hand value (sum of cards in one suit) at the end of the round. Players start with 3 'lives'.
rules.gameplay:
1. The dealer can swap their hand for 'The Window' before revealing it to the group.
2. In turn, players can: - **Swap ONE**: Exchange one hand card with one center card. - **Swap ALL**: Exchange the entire hand. - **Pass**: Do nothing for the turn. - **Close (Knock)**: Signal the final round. All other players get ONE more turn.
3. **Hosa Aba (31)**: If a player reaches 31, they reveal immediately and the round ends instantly.
keyRules: Follow the legal action constraints defined for Hosa Aba.
Round outcome is resolved by the scoring method: - Only cards of the SAME SUIT are summed.
Winning condition: Avoid having the lowest hand value (sum of cards in one suit) at the end of the round.

strategy.basic: Always aim for 31 by collecting the Ace and two 10-value cards of the same suit. If you have 30.5 (three of a kind), it is a very strong defensive hand.
strategy.intermediate: Closing the round (Knocking) is a power move. Only do it if you have 25+ points and think others have much less.
strategy.advanced: Watch what others take from the 'Window'. If an opponent takes a Rose, don't lead Roses unless you are dumping high cards you don't need.
tips: Collect Obers and Unders of the suit you have an Ace in.
If the window has no cards of your suit, consider 'swapping all' to disrupt opponents' strategies.

scoring.description: When the play is over, all the players' cards are exposed.
